title: T'Boli Tribe [cite: 131]
summary_statement: Indigenous dream-weavers of South Mindanao whose bamboo music is a sacred dialogue between nature and their spiritual beliefs. [cite: 134]
full_content: The T'boli are among the most celebrated indigenous groups in the Philippines, centered in the highland lake complex of Sebu, Selutan, and Lahit. [cite: 135]
They are world-famous for their T'nalak textile, woven by "dream weavers" who receive patterns in their sleep. [cite: 136]
Their musical culture is equally rich and deeply connected to their worldview; [cite: 137]
they have specific instruments played during a lunar eclipse to call upon a warrior to slay the creature swallowing the moon. [cite: 138]
This culture is exceptionally well-preserved, with even the T'boli youth actively participating in the practice of their traditional songs and instruments. [cite: 139]
The T'boli ensemble features a wide array of specialized instruments, including the Sludoy (polychordal zither), the Kumbing (jaw harp), and the Tnonggong (barrel drum). [cite: 140]
The Tnonggong is typically played by males and is covered with deer, goat, or horse skin; [cite: 141]
it is a sacred object, and "stepping over" it is strictly prohibited as it is believed to result in the enlargement of the breast or scrotum. [cite: 142]
For leisure and entertainment, they play the Dwegey, a single-stringed bowed lute with a neck made of bamboo and a resonator fashioned from a coconut shell. [cite: 143]
Their craft process involves ancient preservation techniques like smoking the bamboo to ensure durability. [cite: 144]
They utilize  Bambusa spinosa  for their Sludoy and Kumbing, while the larger Tnonggong and the neck of the Dwegey are made from Afus bamboo ( Dendrocalamus asper ). [cite: 145]
The Kumbing is often protected by a specialized bamboo case called a  sokong . [cite: 146]

For their flutes like the Sloli and Hlendeg, they use "seben" bamboo and create intricate designs by slightly burning the wood with hot metal, often depicting patterns inspired by insects and the surrounding forest. [cite: 147]

quote.text: "Our music expresses what we feel, attracts the cold air in the heat, and speaks for the nature that surrounds us." [cite: 148]
